answersReview: Review 5720252758 at ee131f72, changes requested: five correctness defects and thirteen maintainability findings, all eighteen threads answered and resolved, plus the bun.lock revert the review asked for. Code head a395dc20852a1a8c25d8ee64a0131a0ba639724f.

proof.criterion: Defect 1: with the reading pane on, Enter on a list control (a row's owner link, Later (n), the bulk bar, a filter) is that control's, not a jump into the selected question's answer box.
proof.surface: The Inbox at pane width, rendered with its real keymap, where the reviewer's own probe found the defect.
proof.command: cd packages/dispatch && bun test web/src/features/inbox/Inbox.test.tsx -t "Enter is the link's or the button's"
proof.observed: Green: the focused link and the focused filter button each receive Enter (fireEvent.keyDown answers true, the default not prevented) and keep the focus, and a row's own Enter still reaches the answer box.
proof.negativeControl: With the old `when` restored (`paneShown ? !focusInPane() && …`) the row fails: `expect(fireEvent.keyDown(link, { key: "Enter" })).toBe(true)` receives false, which is the keymap having taken the key and called preventDefault.

proof.criterion: Defect 2: in a document with several open decision blocks, 1-9 and Enter act on the selected block, not on the first open block in document order.
proof.surface: The same Inbox, with two answerable decision cards drawn in the column.
proof.command: cd packages/dispatch && bun test web/src/features/inbox/Inbox.test.tsx -t "the answer keys act on the selected decision block"
proof.observed: Green: two decision asks of one document, ?item= naming the second, `1` ticking the second block's first option and Enter opening its note disclosure while the first block's stays shut.
proof.negativeControl: With the lookups restored to the whole pane the row fails: `1` ticks the first block's option, and the wait on the selected card's option times out.

proof.criterion: Defect 3: Change answer then Cancel leaves no draft behind, so no card claims a recorded answer was never sent.
proof.command: cd packages/dispatch && bun test web/src/features/inbox/AskCard.test.tsx -t "Change answer"
proof.observed: Green: after Change answer and Cancel there is no 'closed before you sent your answer' line and no leftover draft, so the column no longer holds that question either.
proof.negativeControl: The reviewer's probe is the control: before the fix it printed `BANNER: This question closed before you sent your answer, so it was not sent. Your text is here to copy.First note` over the reader's own recorded answer, on every card for that ask.

proof.criterion: Defect 4: an approval's word marks land on their own characters, with a hard break before them.
proof.surface: The editor's change decorations, built against a real ProseMirror document.
proof.observed: 220 pass, 0 fail, including the new hard-break case: a decoration over `canary` after a `\n` draws `canary`, where it drew `anary ` before.
proof.negativeControl: The reviewer's probe: `"Line one  \nthe canary word."` has textContent `"Line one\nthe canary word."`, one character per break, which `textRuns` did not count; the new case fails without the leafText advance.

proof.criterion: Defect 5: the word diff is bounded, so two unrelated large blocks cannot hold the main thread.
proof.surface: The pairing module both surfaces read.
proof.observed: Green, with a row for a pair past the bound: the pair is drawn as one whole-block removal and one whole-block addition rather than word by word. Measured here with diff@9: unbounded 1000 words 655 ms and 3000 words 7.7 s; bounded, the worst case is about 113 ms, and a tenth of a 3000-word block changed still diffs word by word (47 ms).
proof.negativeControl: The reviewer's benchmark is the control for the unbounded path: 679 ms at 1000 words, 8.1 s at 3000, 39 s at 6000.

proof.criterion: The reading pane, the change view and the keys still behave as the spec says, after five fixes and thirteen refactors.
proof.surface: The Inbox page and the document pages of a running Dispatch - the built SPA served by the real Go server against a real Postgres, driven in a real Chromium - at 1440, 1280, 1279 and 390 px and in the drawer.
proof.command: source /legion/harness/env.sh && cd packages/dispatch && bun run e2e -- e2e/inbox-reading-pane.e2e.ts e2e/inbox.e2e.ts e2e/inbox-drawer.e2e.ts e2e/keyboard-inbox.e2e.ts e2e/keyboard.e2e.ts e2e/doc.e2e.ts e2e/artifacts.e2e.ts --project=chromium
proof.observed: 88 passed. The eight rows of inbox-reading-pane.e2e.ts are among them, unmodified, two of them the tester's.
proof.negativeControl: Each of the two behaviour changes among the refactors carries its own red-before row: Next change offered where no mark drew (the button was there before the guard), and `j` from a held question (it selected the first row before the fix).

proof.criterion: Everything static is green here before the push, and CI runs on the code head.
proof.surface: The repository's own gates, and GitHub Actions.
proof.command: bunx biome check packages/dispatch/ packages/proof-editor/; bun run typecheck and bun run test in each package; gh api 'repos/sjawhar/legion/actions/runs?head_sha=a395dc20…'
proof.observed: biome `Checked 778 files, No fixes applied`; proof-editor typecheck clean and 220 pass 0 fail; dispatch typecheck clean and 3060 pass 0 fail. GitHub created CI run 41161396138 for this head, queued when read; I did not wait for it, as the daemon reads CI itself.

a395dc20852a - bun.lock back to the base's copy
trickyParts: bun.lock in this workspace is rewritten by every `bun install`: the base's copy records older workspace versions for envoy-plugin, pi-envoy and pi-legion than their package.json files carry, so bun corrects it each time even when it installs nothing. The commit keeps the base's copy; after any install, restore it (`jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" restore --from <the merge base> bun.lock`) before committing or pushing, and note that `jj restore --from main@origin` is wrong once main has moved past the merge base.

The two behaviour changes hidden among the refactors are the ones to re-read: Next change is now offered only while the drawn version carries marked blocks, and `j` from a question held past its row steps on from where that row stood. Both carry their own unit row.

Both fixes narrow the keys to the selected ask's own card.
